title: Doubling the last letter before adding -ing, -ed or -er
canonical_examples_source: Language rules self-verified; format ref: bank uk-ks2-2024-gps (KS2 GPS).

blocks.content: When you add -ing or -ed to a short word, sometimes you double the last letter first. Let's learn exactly when to do it.
For a short word ending in one vowel then one consonant, double the final consonant before adding an ending that starts with a vowel (like -ing, -ed, -er).

steps: 'run' ends in one vowel (u) then one consonant (n).

blocks.explain: 'hop' ends in one vowel then one consonant, so double the p and add -ed: hopped.
blocks.rule: For a short word ending in one vowel then one consonant, double the last consonant before -ing, -ed or -er.

blocks.content: Do NOT double when the word ends in two consonants (jump) or has two vowels before the consonant (rain).

blocks.question: Which spelling is correct?
blocks.explain: 'jump' ends in two consonants (m, p), so you do not double — just add -ing: jumping.
blocks.rule: Do not double the last consonant when the word ends in two consonants or has two vowels before the consonant.

blocks.question: Ann writes 'runing' for run + ing. Why is it wrong, and what is the rule?
options: Double the final n: 'running' — a short vowel and one final consonant double before -ing
blocks.explain: 'run' has one short vowel (u) and one final consonant (n). Before an ending that starts with a vowel, like -ing, you double that consonant: running. This keeps the vowel short.
blocks.rule: One short vowel + one final consonant: double the consonant before a vowel ending.
blocks.principle: Doubling the consonant protects the short vowel sound.
canonical_solution: 'run' = short vowel u + single consonant n

rubric.look_for: checks the vowel and final consonant of 'run'
doubles the n to get running
explains doubling keeps the vowel short

misconceptions.coach: One short vowel plus one consonant means double: running.
Double only once: running, not runnning.

blocks.content: So: one vowel + one consonant means double it; two consonants or two vowels means leave it. Time to practise!
